A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HIS-QA, HIS-Bench and HIS-GPT work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite supplementary-material reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original HIS-Bench evaluations, component and training ablations, input-format comparisons and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds human quality assessments, evaluator-validation results and fine-tuned baseline evaluations.

M1.justification: The scene and motion encoders, AInt auxiliary objectives, LTP encoding, frozen backbone and two-stage HIS-GPT training remain unchanged. The additional experiments do not introduce a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly evaluates 100 OpenEQA samples in a human assessment of benchmark quality; v1 only discussed OpenEQA. HIS-GPT's training datasets and the 800-question HIS-Bench task coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The HIS-QA comparator methods remain unchanged. New Table 8 evaluates existing Chat-Scene, LLaVA-OV and LLaVA-OV+GPT-4 baselines under additional fine-tuning conditions. Qwen2.5-7B is introduced as an evaluator, not a competing HIS-QA method.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantial evaluation protocols: three-person, four-dimension ratings of all HIS-Bench samples and 100 OpenEQA samples; human assessment of GPT-4o answers; alternative judging with Qwen2.5-7B; and baseline fine-tuning using converted HIS-GPT training data. These supplement the retained original evaluation.

E4.justification: New Appendices A.4–A.5 investigate benchmark quality and evaluator validity, while D.1 tests whether the comparison survives baseline fine-tuning. These address questions absent from v1's analyses. Existing component, loss-weight, LoRA and video-format ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.5 adds Pearson correlation estimates for human–GPT and cross-evaluator agreement, and the human studies report three raters. The original three-evaluation averaging remains unchanged; no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Original performance and ablation results remain unchanged, including HIS-GPT's 48.7 average. New Table 8 reports fine-tuned baseline scores of 13.4, 19.7 and 20.8. Table 5 adds human quality ratings, including correctness scores of 4.35 for HIS-Bench and 4.64 for OpenEQA. Appendix A.5 adds correlations of 0.54 and 0.75, and Table 6 adds Qwen-judged scores. These are additional results under new protocols.

T1.justification: The task formulation, model equations, losses and spatial definitions are unchanged. The added empirical correlation analysis introduces no new theoretical result, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same central claims: introducing HIS-QA and HIS-Bench, proposing a joint human-scene foundation model, and achieving superior HIS-QA performance. The new appendix evidence supports these retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets human ratings as validating benchmark quality, evaluator correlations as demonstrating accuracy and reproducibility, and the remaining fine-tuned baseline gap as supporting unified 3D modeling. Existing interpretations of AInt, LTP, frozen-LLM training and rendered inputs are retained.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a repository address for a planned code and data release. Appendix D.1 identifies reuse and format conversion of HIS-GPT training data for baselines, but supplies no detailed fine-tuning recipe. Existing implementation settings and prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 72 referenced works and the same positioning relative to scene-only and human-only understanding are retained. The added studies reuse existing citations without revising the central novelty argument.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is unchanged. v2 updates affiliations and contact information, lightly rewrites the conclusion, adds acknowledgements and appendix subsections, and places the appendices before the bibliography instead of using a separately headed supplement.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5, 6 and 8, adjusts figure sizing and placement, and reflows supplementary figures alongside the relocated bibliography. Existing supplementary Figures S1–S13 become Figures 6–18; their substantive contents and existing result displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 did not quantify benchmark quality or human–judge agreement and compared trained HIS-GPT with zero-shot baselines. v2's human assessments, alternative-evaluator checks and matched-corpus baseline fine-tuning address central validation and fairness gaps, substantially strengthening the empirical foundation. The 0.54 human correlation warrants more cautious interpretation than the paper gives it, and fine-tuning details remain sparse, but the added evidence provides a substantial net benefit.
